en: The Ritual for the Supreme Repentance of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*,
compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhili of Siming, based on the Tiantai teachings and contemplations transmitted from the Song dynasty.
All pay homage with reverence.

With single-minded devotion, prostrate once before the eternally abiding Triple Gem of the ten directions. Having completed this one prostration, kneel with the right knee on the ground and hold the incense burner, saying:
"May these clouds of incense and flowers pervade the worlds of the ten directions."
I make offerings to all Buddhas,
the Honored Dharma, and all Bodhisattvas,
as well as the assemblies of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.
And all celestial seers:
having performed these acts of Buddha-work, and having made offerings with all reverence and prostrated once, they again kneel and entreat, saying:
"With a single mind, we entreat: Namo to our Original Teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha."
In the east is Akṣobhya, the fourth Buddha, the World-Honored One;
together with Ratnakusuma, Vaidūryaprabhāsaśrī,
and all other Buddhas throughout the *Suvarṇabhāsottama-sūtra* and across the ten directions and three periods of time, they make three requests and one prostration.
With single-minded devotion, I take refuge in the *Mahāyāna Suvarṇaprabhāsottama Sūtra*, the ocean of the twelve divisions of the scriptures; having made this request three times, I prostrate once.
With single-minded devotion, I take refuge in the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva,
and Suvarṇaprabhāsa Bodhisattva.

The Bodhisattva Kancanagarbha, ever compassionate toward the Dharma, having received the three requests from all the Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and the assembly of worthy and holy ones throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time within the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, prostrated once.
With single-minded devotion, we take refuge in and entreat the Great Brahmā Deva,
the Four World-Protecting Kings of the Heaven of the Thirty-three,
and the Vajra Secret-Keeper, General Saṃjñeya.
The Great Eloquence Deity (Mahāpratisarā), the Mārīcī Deity,
and the Vaiśravaṇa Deity.
The Earth Goddess Sthāvarā,
the Bodhi Tree Goddess,
Hārītī the Mother of Demons, and her five hundred retinues.
All these are great bodhisattvas and the like,
as well as all the numinous shrines of the famous mountains and great rivers within this country,
and the spirits and deities belonging to the territories of this province.
In this dwelling place, the guardian deity of the monastery who upholds the True Dharma and all the assembly of noble ones should not be prostrated to after three requests have been made.
With single-minded devotion, we offer our invocation: Namo to the Great Goddess of Merit, who possesses supreme majesty and accomplishes all matters.
In this stage, after the assembly has chanted the three requests, they do not prostrate;
however, laypeople must prostrate.
One should join the palms and recite the mantra.
Namo Śrī-mahādevī. Tadyathā: *tici-ti-je-niya*. (The third [syllable] is pronounced with both [vowels];
*paripūrṇa-cche*). *Pū* is pronounced as *phu*.
Zhé (pronounced with the initial *ch* and final *-e*): *zhē lì chū qiè*. Zhé (pronounced with the initial *sh* and final *-i*): *zhé shì liè qiè*.
Lèi (pronounced with the initial *l* and final *-ě*): *lèi lì jì qiè*.
The four [mantras] are all identical: *Samantabhadra* (the *ra* is pronounced with a *cha* cut; the *ni* is a departing tone).

*Mahā-vijayā-rajñī* (the *ra* is pronounced with a *cha* cut; the *ni* is a departing tone). *Mahā-bhīṣmā-rakṣa-pratīhāraṇī-tarkā* (the *ta* is pronounced with a *cha* cut). *Sarvārtha-sādhani-artha-supratibhā* (the *a* is pronounced with a *ge* cut). *Āyana-dharma-dā-mahā-vikubhitā-mahā-mitrā upasaṃkhyeti* (the *u* is pronounced with a *gu* cut).

*Hī* (pronounced with the *qiè* of *xiāngqì*), *Tiḍi* (pronounced with the *qiè* of *liǎoxī*), *Mahākṣe* (the *kṣe* pronounced with the *qiè* of *hùjié*), *Susaṃkriḍe*, *Samantaprabhe*, *Anupariniḥśvāha*. Recite this seven times.
The Buddha’s face is like the pure, full moon, And like a thousand suns emitting radiant light;
His eyes are pure, long, and wide like blue lotuses, His teeth are white, even, and closely set like jade or snow.
The Buddha’s virtues are boundless like the great ocean, With infinite wondrous jewels accumulated within.
The water of wisdom and virtue is ever full; hundreds of thousands of supreme concentrations completely fill [you].
The marks of the wheels upon your soles are all adorned, with hubs, rims, and a thousand spokes all perfectly even.
Your hands and feet are universally graced with webbing, fully endowed with the characteristics like those of the king of geese.

The Buddha’s body radiates brilliance like a mountain of gold; Pure, extraordinary, and without peer, it is like Mount Sumeru, replete with merit. Therefore, I bow my head to the King of the Buddha-mountain;
His marks and signs are as unfathomable as space, Surpassing a thousand suns in the emission of light.
All are like flames and illusions, inconceivable; therefore, I prostrate with a mind free from attachment.
Having offered this praise, I shall now set forth my intention.
One should join the palms in reverence.
Instruct the assembly to chant three times in a level tone:
"Namo to the Buddha Ratnakusumavairocana;
Namo to the Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Golden Light."
"Namo to the Great Goddess of Merit who accomplishes all matters through supreme majesty. Having recited this three times,
one should next present offerings while focusing the mind on her as if facing her directly.
Subsequently, one should recite the verses;
at other times, these are omitted.
Food and drink must be pure and prepared in accordance with the Dharma.
Furthermore, regarding the words "holding and scattering," one should simply say,
"Incense and flowers... until the attainment of the Perfect Universal Wisdom (Samantabhadra-jñāna)," and then immediately prostrate to the Buddha.
Now, in my place of practice, I have prepared offerings and lit various lamps and burned various incenses.
He offered various kinds of food and drink,
pure and prepared according to the Dharma,
respectfully holding them forth as an offering to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
The Mahāyāna sūtras,
the Bodhisattvas, the Sages, and all the Three Jewels;
furthermore, separately prepare incense, flowers, food, and drink.
I dedicate this merit to Mahādeva and Mahāprajñā,
the Four Heavenly Kings, Brahmā and Śakra,
and the noble assembly of the eight classes of devas, nāgas, and others.
Furthermore, take food and drink and scatter them toward other directions as offerings to the various spirits;
I pray that the Triple Gem and the celestial immortals [will accept this].
Have compassion for me and all sentient beings;
accept this offering through the power of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* and the majestic spiritual authority of all Buddhas.
In a single thought-moment, they manifest all Buddha-fields of the ten directions,
pervading them like clouds and moistening them everywhere like rain;
they extensively perform Buddha-works to equally permeate and transform sentient beings.
"May we together realize the wisdom of the universal Buddha-nature by generating the bodhicitta"—this too should be recited according to one's inclination;
it need not necessarily be this specific phrase.
Having spoken these words, [one should proceed].
One should take the food and drink to a clean place outside the ritual arena and scatter them in the four directions,
first speaking these words:
I now, in accordance with the teachings, make offerings to the Triple Gem of the Mahāyāna and to the Auspicious Great Deity (Mahādeva).
Taking these various foods and drinks,
I scatter and sprinkle them in all directions as universal gifts to all the deities.
May all the deities possess sovereign power and authority;
may they gather universally in a single thought-moment and each receive the Dharma-food,
becoming fully satisfied without lack, their physical strength courageous and keen.
"May you protect me with steadfastness and know my aspirations.

I pray that we may together dedicate this merit so that it may universally moisten all sentient beings, such that their karmic fruits may naturally result in the constant enjoyment of supreme bliss. Having thus made this prayer of dedication, he concluded.
Even when scattering food in the four directions,
one should visualize that immeasurable spirits and deities all come to receive the food;
at that time, one may recite the aforementioned mantra.
Alternatively, one may simply recite "Namo Śrī Mahādevī" and take the exhaustion of the food as the limit.
Once the scattering and sprinkling are finished,
one returns to the maṇḍala to pay homage to the Buddha.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to our original teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to Akṣobhya Buddha of the East.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to Ratnaśrī Buddha of the South.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Buddha Amitāyus of the Western Quarter.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Buddha Subhavyūha of the Northern Quarter.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Buddha Ratnakusumaprabhāsasikhin.
With single-minded devotion, pay homage to the Buddha Ratnaśrī.
With single-minded devotion, pay homage to the Buddha Vimalajvalanaratnaprabhāsa-rāja-lakṣaṇa.
With single-minded devotion, pay homage to the Buddha Suvarṇajvālāprabha.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Buddha Golden Hundred Radiant Illuminating Treasury.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Buddha Golden Mountain Jewel Canopy.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Buddha Golden Flower Flame Light Mark.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Buddha Mahārcis.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Buddha Ratnākara.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all Buddhas throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time, as mentioned in the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate three times to the Mahāyāna *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, the ocean of the twelve divisions of the scriptures.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Suvarṇaprabhāsa.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Suvarṇagarbha.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Constant Compassion.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Dharma-Supreme.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas within the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra* and throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Sangha of worthy and holy ones— the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and others.
For the sake of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma realm,
I pray that they may completely sever the three obstacles.
Taking refuge and repenting with one prostration while visualizing the ten minds of the direct and reverse order:
I, Bhikṣu [Name], take refuge and pay supreme homage to all Buddhas currently residing throughout the ten directions.
Having already attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi,
they turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma and uphold the illuminating wheel of Dharma.
They rain down the great Dharma rain;
they beat the great Dharma drum;
they blow the great Dharma conch.
They raise the great banner of the Dharma and hold aloft the great torch of the Dharma,
desiring to bring benefit, welfare, and happiness to all sentient beings.
They constantly practice the gift of Dharma to guide and advance the deluded multitudes,
so that they may attain the great fruit and realize eternal bliss.
In this manner, all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, employ their body, speech, and mind.
I bow my head in sincere devotion;
with utmost sincerity, I pay homage to all those World-Honored Ones,
by means of true wisdom and the true eye.
Truthfully realizing true equality,
they fully know and fully see the wholesome and unwholesome karma of all sentient beings.
Since beginningless birth and death, I have...
They follow along with the flow of evil,
together with all sentient beings they create karmic obstructions and transgressions,
and are bound and fettered by greed, hatred, and delusion.
When one has not yet known the Buddha,
not yet known the Dharma,
and not yet known the Sangha.
Unaware of what is virtuous and what is non-virtuous,
they committed crimes of immediate retribution through their body, speech, and mind,
and with an evil intent, they shed the blood of a Buddha.
Slandering the true Dharma,
causing schism in the Saṃgha,
and killing an Arhat.
They commit the three physical, four verbal, and three mental types of conduct, thereby performing the ten unwholesome karmas, such as killing one's father and mother.
Performing [evil deeds] oneself, inciting others to do so,
rejoicing in seeing them performed,
and groundlessly slandering virtuous people.
They deceive with scales and measures, taking the false for the true;
they give impure food and drink to all beings,
including their parents within the six realms of existence.
They further afflict and harm one another;
some even steal the property of stūpas or the property belonging to the Saṃgha from the four quarters.
They used the property of the *saṃgha* present before them as they pleased,
and did not joyfully practice the Dharma and Vinaya of the World-Honored One.
They do not comply with the instructions of their teachers and preceptors;
upon seeing practitioners of the Śrāvaka, Pratyekabuddha, or Mahāyāna vehicles,
they take pleasure in reviling and insulting them.
They cause those who practice conditioned phenomena to give rise to remorse and distress;
upon seeing those superior to themselves, they harbor jealousy;
and regarding the gift of Dharma and material gifts, they constantly give rise to stinginess and attachment.
Enshrouded by ignorance, their minds deluded by false views,
they fail to cultivate wholesome causes and allow evil to increase;
they give rise to slander toward all Buddhas.
To preach what is not the Dharma as the Dharma, and to preach the Dharma as what is not the Dharma—
such various offenses [the Buddha perceives] with his true wisdom and true eye.
This is the true proof.
I truly know and truly see all things in their equality.
I now take refuge before all the Buddhas.
I reveal them all and dare not conceal them.
As for sins not yet committed, I shall never commit them again;
as for sins already committed, I now repent of them all.
Whatever karmic obstructions I have committed that should cause me to fall into the evil realms— the hells, the animal kingdom, or the realm of hungry ghosts;
among the asura hosts or the eight inopportune states—
may all such karmic obstructions in this life of mine be completely extinguished.
All retributions for evil shall not be experienced in the future.
Just as all the great bodhisattvas of the past cultivated the practices of enlightenment,
so too have I fully repented all karmic obstructions.
I now also repent of my karmic obstructions.
I confess them all openly and dare not conceal them;
may the sins already committed be extinguished.
I shall not dare to commit further evil in the future.
Just as all the great Bodhisattvas of the future cultivate the practices for enlightenment,
I have now fully repented of all my karmic obstructions.
I now also repent of my karmic obstructions.
I disclose them all and dare not conceal them;
may the sins already committed be extinguished.
I shall not dare to commit further evil in the future.
Just as the great bodhisattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions in the present cultivate the practices of enlightenment,
I likewise confess all my karmic obstructions.
I now also repent of my karmic obstructions.
I confess them all openly and dare not conceal them.
May the sins already committed be extinguished.
I dare not commit further evil in the future; having repented, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
I, Bhikṣu [Name], take refuge in and prostrate my head before all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, throughout the ten directions.
To all those World-Honored Ones who, having first attained perfect enlightenment and not yet turned the wheel of Dharma,
desire to relinquish their response bodies and enter nirvana—
to them all I pay homage with my head bowed.

Exhorting [the Buddhas] to turn the Wheel of Dharma and requesting that they remain long in the world to deliver, liberate, and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings; having thus made this request, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
I, the bhikṣu [Name], take refuge in and prostrate my head to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, throughout the ten directions.
I now rejoice in the roots of goodness cultivated through the three karmas of giving, precept-keeping, and mental wisdom by all sentient beings;
in the roots of goodness of the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas, and noble sages;
and in the Dharma of the wondrous Bodhi realized by the Buddhas of the ten directions.
I wholeheartedly rejoice in and praise all the merit of every gift.
Having rejoiced, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
I, the bhikṣu [Name], take refuge in and prostrate my head before all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, throughout the ten directions.
May you bear witness:
from beginningless time until this day,
all the various virtues cultivated by my three karmas.
Generosity, ethical discipline, and wisdom;
up to and including confession, entreaty, and sympathetic joy—
these are gathered in the present.

I dedicate this to all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, that they may together realize Bodhi as do all Buddhas. Having performed this dedication, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Triple Gem.
I, the bhikṣu [Name], take refuge in and prostrate my head to all the World-Honored Buddhas of the ten directions.
May you bear witness to my humble sincerity and manifest my present aspiration.
May the eight classes of devas increase in majestic power and come constantly to protect and sustain this land of mine.
The winds are auspicious and the rains favorable; grains and fruits ripen in abundance.
The Sage Emperor and Benevolent King presides with compassion over boundless realms;
his ministers and officials constantly maintain their honorable dignity.
May the myriad people and the four classes of society abide forever in peace,
prosperity, and joy. May the Buddhas and Dharma, the donors, parents, teachers, and monks,
as well as all sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm— including those who have been enemies or kin over successive lifetimes— likewise find peace.
May all give rise to right faith and resolve for Bodhicitta;
may they cultivate the six perfections in unison and fully equip themselves with the two adornments.
Furthermore, may we pray that all the sages grant their secret assistance.
May I always encounter the Mahāyāna and spiritual friends who open my Buddha-wisdom.
May my vows and practices manifest before me so that I may bear the burden of its propagation.
May I use the Buddha-dharma of the three periods of time to guide and transform all beings.
Thus, having made the vow to kindle the lamp of inexhaustibility so that all sentient beings may together return to the secret treasury, one takes refuge and pays homage to the Triple Gem:
Namo Buddha. Namo Dharma.
Homage to the Sangha.
Homage to our Original Teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha.
Homage to the Four Buddhas of the Four Directions.
Homage to the Buddha Ratnakusumaruciraprabhāsa.
Homage to the Mahāyāna Suvarṇaprabhāsottama Sūtra. Three times, homage to the Bodhisattva Śraddhālakṣaṇa.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Suvarṇaprabhāsa.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Suvarṇagarbha.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Nityakaruṇā.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Dharmottara. Homage to the Great Goddess Mahāpuṇyavatī, who possesses supreme majesty and accomplishes all matters.
I take refuge in the Buddha;
may all beings realize the Great Way and give rise to the unsurpassed mind.
I take refuge in the Dharma.
When taking refuge in the Sangha, one should wish that all beings enter deeply into the treasury of the scriptures, their wisdom as vast as the ocean.
One should wish that all beings preside over great assemblies, managing them all without hindrance.
Homage to the Noble Assembly.
The Ritual for the Repentance of the Suvarṇaprabhāsa-uttama-sūtra.
